rules.title: Cap on upfront payments and security deposit (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or agent may not require more than first month's rent, last month's rent at the same rate, a security deposit equal to the first month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. The lessor must deposit the security deposit as required and give the tenant a statement of condition.
rules.key_value: First month's rent + last month's rent + security deposit of 1 month's rent + key and lock cost

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential leases and tenancies in Massachusetts, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Does not apply to a lease, rental, occupancy or tenancy of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: Lease provisions conflicting with the section, and tenant waivers of it, are void as against public policy.
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Optional fee in lieu of security deposit (regulations authorized)
rules.requirement: The executive office of housing and livable communities may issue regulations letting a lessor and tenant agree to a fee in place of a security deposit. Such regulations must make the fee optional and cap the total of fee and deposit at 1 month's rent.
rules.key_value: Total of fees plus security deposit not to exceed 1 month's rent

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts, subject to regulations to be promulgated by the executive office; vacation rentals of 100 days or less excluded.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: A lessor who offers the fee must offer it to every approved prospective tenant regardless of income, race, gender, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, immigration status, household size or credit score.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Fee may be wholly or partly non-refundable with written disclosure and tenant acknowledgment; tenant may opt out by paying the security deposit; the executive office must consult the attorney general before promulgating regulations.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: The fee scheme operates only through regulations that the executive office may promulgate; the text does not show whether they have been issued.
rules.quoted_span: provided, however, that the executive office of housing and livable communities may promulgate regulations to authorize a lessor and a tenant or prospective tenant to agree to the payment of a fee in lieu of payment of a security deposit
rules.conflict_note: The statute only authorizes regulations. The document does not say whether implementing regulations have been issued, so the fee option may not yet be operational.

rules.title: Security deposit return within 30 days; permitted deductions
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the lessor must return the security deposit or any balance. Deductions are allowed only for unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid real estate tax increases under a conforming tax escalation clause, and reasonable repair of tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear. Damage deductions require a sworn itemized list with cost evidence within the 30 days.
rules.key_value: 30 days to return deposit or itemized list of damages

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies-at-will and written leases in Massachusetts, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Damage listed in the move-in statement of condition cannot be deducted unless repaired and then re-damaged by the tenant.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;

rules.title: Security deposit held in separate interest-bearing bank account
rules.requirement: Security deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, beyond creditors' claims and transferable to a subsequent owner. The tenant must receive a receipt naming the bank and account within 30 days, or may demand immediate return of the deposit.
rules.key_value: Separate interest-bearing account; receipt within 30 days

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential lessors who receive security deposits in Massachusetts, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor

rules.title: Annual interest on security deposits
rules.requirement: A lessor holding a deposit for one year or longer must pay the tenant interest at 5% per year, or the lesser amount actually received from the bank, at the end of each year of the tenancy. The lessor must also give an annual statement identifying the bank and account.
rules.key_value: 5% per year or lesser amount received from the bank

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts where the deposit is held one year or longer, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies where the lessor holds the deposit for one year or longer from the start of the tenancy.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy.

rules.title: Move-in statement of condition for security deposits
rules.requirement: A lessor who accepts a security deposit must give the tenant a separate signed written statement of the premises' condition, listing existing damage, within 10 days after the tenancy starts or on receipt of the deposit, whichever is later. The statement must carry a prescribed bold notice, and the tenant may return a separate list of damages.
rules.key_value: Statement of condition within 10 days of tenancy commencement

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential lessors accepting security deposits in Massachusetts, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.interaction: Damage listed in the statement cannot later be deducted from the deposit (see subsection 4).
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented.

rules.title: Treble damages and forfeiture for security deposit violations
rules.requirement: A lessor who fails to hold the deposit properly, to transfer it to a successor, or to return it on time forfeits the right to retain any of it. The tenant is then awarded three times the deposit owed plus 5% interest, court costs and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: 3x the deposit plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential lessors holding security deposits in Massachusetts, except vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Applies on violation of clauses (a), (d) or (e) of subsection 6: failure to deposit funds properly, to transfer the deposit to a successor, or to return the deposit within 30 days.

rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent from the date when such payment became due, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
